Rumors suggest Apple will announce new products on October 13. Based on the timing of past October events, here's a timeline of when Apple might announce the event date.

Will Apple hold an October event?

Apple's September events are relatively fixed in timing, but October events are harder to predict, with both the event date and announcement time difficult to pin down.

Since 2010, Apple has held only ten October events, the most recent being the Halloween-themed "Scary Fast" event on the evening of October 30, 2023.

Here's a回顾 of how many days in advance Apple has announced each October event since 2010:

Year Event Announcement date Event date 2023 “Scary Fast” Tuesday, October 24 Monday, October 30 2021 “Unleashed” Tuesday, October 12 Monday, October 18 2020 “Hi, Speed” Tuesday, October 6 Tuesday, October 13 2018 “There’s more in the making” Thursday, October 18 Tuesday, October 30 2016 “Hello again” Wednesday, October 19 Thursday, October 27 2014 “It’s been way too long” Wednesday, October 8 Thursday, October 16 2013 “We still have a lot to cover” Tuesday, October 15 Tuesday, October 22 2012 “We’ve got a little more to show you” Tuesday, October 16 Tuesday, October 23 2011 “Let’s talk iPhone” Tuesday, September 27 Tuesday, October 4 2010 “Back to the Mac” Wednesday, October 13 Wednesday, October 20

That said, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple plans to launch the long-rumored smart home hub, next-generation HomePod mini, and Apple TV 4K with new Siri AI features on Tuesday, October 13, but did not reveal whether Apple would hold a launch event for these products.

If true, Apple could announce the event date as early as Monday, October 5, or as late as Wednesday, October 7.

It's worth noting that Apple is also expected to launch an iPad mini with an OLED display, a new iMac, and several new MacBook Pro models (including one with a touchscreen) in 2026. Whether these products will be announced at the same event, a separate event, or simply via press release remains unknown.

Looking back, Apple released new Mac products via press release over three consecutive days in October 2024; in October 2025, without holding an event, it launched the M5 chip along with new iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, and Apple Vision Pro models.

By comparison, Apple has held only one November event — the "One More Thing" event in November 2020, which debuted Mac computers powered by the M1 Apple Silicon chip.

Of course, 2020 was a rather special year for Apple's event schedule. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Apple broke with tradition by holding WWDC at the end of June, followed by events in September and October respectively.

What new products do you think Apple will announce at the rumored October event? Let us know in the comments.
